aboutMeta: Why NextCycle compares newer California water-monitoring evidence with official impaired-waters decisions.
aboutParagraph1: California updates its Clean Water Act section 303(d) list of impaired waters in multi-year cycles. Each cycle reads data up to a cutoff date. Anything sampled after that waits for a later cycle, sometimes four years or more.
aboutParagraph2: That gap matters. Utilities set budgets and monitoring plans around listings. Communities near impaired waters wait for answers that the data may already hold.
aboutParagraph3: NextCycle presents newer public observations as provisional screening. Source quality, station links and policy-table choices need human review; the screen never replaces an official decision.
aboutParagraph4: Utilyst builds NextCycle as water and power infrastructure intelligence. Methods are open, and the screening code is released under the MIT license.

methodIntro: The data and checks are open. This source release is provisional; its station links, QA filters and policy-table choices still need human review.
methodStartBody: This release combines Region 9 Category 5 pairs from the final 2026 Integrated Report with selected Region 3 Category 5 pairs from the final 2024 report.
methodGatherBody: We retain matched CEDEN results before and after the cutoff. The same calibrated QA rule applies on both sides; results that do not meet it remain visible as pending QA.
methodCount: Count the way the policy counts
methodCountBody: We calibrated the screen against five pairs whose station-, source- and date-matched CEDEN counts reproduce the official totals. The remaining source comparisons are shown below and remain provisional.
methodLabelBody: Each pair gets a screening flag. It is shown next to, and never in place of, the official status.
candidateMethod: Listed, with enough samples and few enough exceedances to meet the count-based delisting screen.
stillMethod: Listed, with newer samples outside the criterion more often than the delisting table allows.
underMethod: Listed, but too few samples since the cutoff to run the delisting screen.
technicalCaveat: The thresholds below transcribe the 2015 Listing Policy tables. Their use for these criteria is provisional and awaits reviewer confirmation; they do not replace the State’s full weight-of-evidence review.
policyTablesTitle: Listing Policy tables and sample sizes
listingRule31: For toxicants, adopted 2015 Listing Policy Table 3.1 uses a sample-count-specific threshold. At n = 2–24, at least two exceedances are required for listing evidence; there is no universal 16-sample, zero-exceedance rule.
listingRule32: Table 3.2 applies to conventional and other pollutants. Use the adopted table and pollutant-specific criteria; do not substitute one general threshold.
delistingRule: Table 4.1 (toxicants) requires at least 28 samples for a delisting screen. Table 4.2 (conventional and other) requires at least 26.
allowedTableIntro: Published allowed-exceedance counts used by this screen:
citationGuideCaveat: Follow the source publisher’s citation guidance when available.
countedNewAfter: Only results that meet the provisional eligibility filter are counted; others remain pending.
cutoffConfirm: Other cycle cutoffs are not used by this build.
qaNonDetect: No non-detects occur in the five calibration pairs. Because reporting-limit values are not included to interpret censored results against each criterion, ND, <, DNQ and other non-= qualifiers remain pending.
criterionDescription: The pair records a simplified fixed criterion transcribed from its fact sheet. Averaging periods, seasonal windows and use-specific nuances are not fully represented and require review.
techLimitWeight: Weight-of-evidence considerations, which the Water Boards may use, are not modeled.
techLimitSediment: Sediment, fish tissue and bacteria-specific rules are not modeled.
techLimitSeason: Averaging periods, seasonality and spatial representativeness are simplified.
techLimitProvisional: Monitoring data is provisional and may be revised after publication.
replicateRule: Exact duplicate source rows are collapsed. Both CollectionReplicate and ResultsReplicate must equal 1; other replicate values remain pending and are never averaged.
qaReject: The five exact-match pairs support Passed with BatchVerification=VAC and Unknown data quality with BatchVerification=NR, only when QACode is blank/None. Some review needed, MetaData, other QA combinations and QACodes remain pending; explicit Reject record rows are excluded.
qaCalibrationNote: The calibration windows contain numeric, unqualified results in a water matrix, blank/None QACode and primary replicates. The same rule applies before and after the cutoff. The Unknown/NR combination is included because it reproduces official counts in all five calibration pairs; this does not mean the whole dataset has been reviewed.
